tour.overview:
Doha changed faster than almost any city on earth. Seventy years ago it was a pearling and fishing town of coral-stone houses around a sheltered bay; today its skyline rises across the water from a seven-kilometre seafront, and its museums are among the most talked-about buildings of the century. This private half-day tour shows you both cities, in the order that makes sense: the old trading heart first, then the waterfront, then the new districts built on reclaimed land.

You start in Souq Waqif, the market where Bedouin traders once came to sell livestock, wool and dates at the water's edge. It was carefully rebuilt in its traditional style in the 2000s, and it is still where Qataris buy spices, perfumes, textiles and hunting gear. Next door are the Falcon Souq, where falcons sit hooded on their perches waiting for buyers, and the Camel Pens. A short drive along the Corniche, with a stop at the Dhow Harbour, brings you to the Museum of Islamic Art, I. M. Pei's limestone landmark on its own island, and to MIA Park, the classic viewpoint over the skyline. In the second half you visit Katara Cultural Village, with its Greek-style amphitheatre, mosaic-tiled mosque and pigeon towers, and finish among the yachts and cafés of Porto Arabia on The Pearl-Qatar.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 4 hours (morning or afternoon)
• Start and finish: your hotel in Doha (or Hamad International Airport for a layover)
• Type: private tour with your own car, driver and English-speaking local guide
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Activity level: easy, mostly short walks on flat ground

WHAT YOU SEE
• Souq Waqif, the Falcon Souq and the Camel Pens.
• The Corniche and the wooden dhows of the old harbour.
• The Museum of Islamic Art (outside, or inside if you choose) and MIA Park.
• Katara Cultural Village: the amphitheatre, the Katara Mosque and the pigeon towers.
• The Pearl-Qatar: the Porto Arabia marina and Qanat Quartier.

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
Doha's sights are spread along twenty kilometres of coast and the heat makes walking between them hard for much of the year. A private car with a guide lets you see the old and the new city in a single half day, with time to step inside the places that interest you rather than looking at them from a bus window.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors, stopover and layover travellers with five or more hours in Doha, families, and anyone who wants an overview of the city before exploring on their own.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want sand dunes rather than city streets, choose our desert safari to the Inland Sea. If you have a full day, our North Qatar day trip takes you to the UNESCO site of Al Zubarah and the mangroves of Al Thakhira.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Shoulders and knees should be covered inside the museums and mosques. From May to September go early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Museum tickets are not included: the Museum of Islamic Art charges visitors around 50 QAR.

days.name: Doha City Tour
days.description:
What to expect: a private half day through old and new Doha – Souq Waqif and the falcons, the Corniche and the dhows, the Museum of Islamic Art, Katara and The Pearl.

Your guide and driver collect you from your hotel (or from Hamad International Airport if you are on a layover). The first stop is Souq Waqif, Doha's 'standing market', named after the traders who once sold from the shore without sitting down. Its lanes of mud-plastered walls and wooden beams were rebuilt in the traditional style in the 2000s, and they are still where Qataris buy spices, frankincense, oud perfume, textiles and hunting gear. Your guide takes you through the spice and perfume alleys to the Falcon Souq, where hooded falcons wait on perches for their buyers – a good falcon can be worth more than a car – and, if you are curious, past the Souq Waqif Falcon Hospital and the camel pens.

From the souq you drive along the Corniche, the seven-kilometre seafront around Doha Bay, and stop at the Dhow Harbour, where traditional wooden boats are still moored. The Museum of Islamic Art stands on its own island at the end of the bay: a geometric limestone building by I. M. Pei, opened in 2008, which holds manuscripts, ceramics, metalwork and textiles from Spain to Central Asia. You can visit inside (about one hour) or admire it from MIA Park, the best viewpoint over the West Bay skyline.

The second half of the tour heads north to Katara Cultural Village, a district of galleries and theatres built in a traditional style, with a large amphitheatre facing the sea, the blue-and-gold tiled Katara Mosque and tall pigeon towers. The tour ends on The Pearl-Qatar, an artificial island of marinas and Mediterranean-style streets, with time for a coffee in Porto Arabia or the canals of Qanat Quartier before you are driven back to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:20 – Souq Waqif and the Falcon Souq (about 1 hour).
10:30 – The Corniche and the Dhow Harbour (short stop).
10:50 – Museum of Islamic Art and MIA Park (30 minutes outside, or about 1 hour inside).
12:00 – Katara Cultural Village (about 30 minutes).
12:40 – The Pearl-Qatar, Porto Arabia (about 30 minutes).
13:15 – Return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• An afternoon start (around 15:00) lets you see Souq Waqif when it comes alive at dusk.
• The Museum of Islamic Art is closed on some mornings; your guide adapts the order of the stops.
• For layovers, allow at least five hours between landing and your next flight.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, English-speaking local guide, bottled water, hotel or airport pick-up.
NOT INCLUDED: museum tickets, food and drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose your date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only once your tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Where does the tour start?
faq.answer: At your hotel anywhere in Doha. For a layover we can collect you at Hamad International Airport and bring you back in time for your flight.

faq.question: Can I do this tour during a layover?
faq.answer: Yes, if you have at least five or six hours between flights and your passport allows you to enter Qatar. The tour itself takes about four hours, and we plan the timing around your arrival and departure.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The car, driver and guide are for you and your group only, so you can change the order of the stops or spend longer where you like.

faq.question: Are museum tickets included?
faq.answer: No. The Museum of Islamic Art charges visitors around 50 QAR; your guide can buy tickets on the spot. Souq Waqif, Katara and The Pearl are free.

faq.question: Morning or afternoon?
faq.answer: Mornings are cooler and the museum is quieter. Afternoons end at Souq Waqif or The Pearl at sunset, when the souq is at its liveliest. In summer we recommend an early start or a late afternoon.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Light clothing that covers shoulders and knees, comfortable shoes, sunglasses and a hat. Carry a light layer for the strong air-conditioning indoors.

faq.question: Can we visit the National Museum of Qatar instead?
faq.answer: Yes. Jean Nouvel's 'desert rose' museum can replace or be added to the Museum of Islamic Art. Tell us when booking so we can adjust the timing.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children and older travellers?
faq.answer: Yes. Walks are short and on flat ground, and the car is never far away. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: Can we stop for lunch?
faq.answer: Yes. Souq Waqif has many good restaurants serving Qatari and Middle Eastern food; lunch is not included, and your guide can recommend a place.

faq.question: What languages do the guides speak?
faq.answer: English as standard. Other languages can be arranged on request, depending on availability.

faq.question: When is the best time of year to visit Doha?
faq.answer: November to March, when days are warm and sunny. From June to September temperatures often exceed 40 °C, so tours are best planned early or late in the day.

faq.question: What is your cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Before your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
